reviews.overall: Em đã viết đủ bốn đoạn, chia hai Detail theo mốc 2006 và nêu đúng Australia giảm, Thailand luôn dẫn đầu. Tuy nhiên, câu mở bài và câu đầu Detail 1 đều thiếu động từ “were”, nên Cô yêu cầu em sửa và nộp lại. Em cũng cần đối chiếu bảng trước khi chép số: Thailand năm 2006 là 1,162,356, Australia năm 2003 là 452,163; nhận định Australia năm 2009 thấp nhất toàn bảng không đúng. Overview cần nêu rõ Thailand tăng đến 2006 rồi giảm, thay vì chỉ nói tăng chung.
reviews.dataGrouping: Em chia hai Detail thành 2003–2006 và 2006–2009; cách này phù hợp vì năm 2006 là điểm đổi chiều của Thailand. Detail 1 có so sánh ba nước, nhưng hai số bị chép sai. Detail 2 cần ghi mức cuối của Thailand và so sánh đúng số thấp nhất toàn bảng.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given table compares how many cars made in three countries - namely Argentina, Australia, Thailand over a six-year period commencing from 2003.  
Overall, there was a general increase in the amount of cars made by Argentina and Thailand, with Thailand witnessing the most pronounced rise, while an opposite trend was observed in Australia. Also of note is that Thailand consistently had the highest figures throughout the years.  
To elaborate, in the former half of period, 235088 cars made in Argentina with a subsequent gradual growth to 352759 in 2006. The figures for Thailand also went up, from 735852 to 1162156 during the same period of time. Conversely, in Australia, the number of cars made declined from 452853 to 341268 during this 3-year period.  
During the remaining time of the period, the number of cars made in Australia continued to decrease to 245624 marking the lowest figure of the entire chart. Similarly, the figures for Thailand dropped by around 0,15 million in three years. A growth was, otherwise, recorded in the figures for Argentina, yet less noticable, from 352759 to 466089 cars.

The table compares how many cars were manufactured in Argentina, Australia and Thailand in 2003, 2006 and 2009.

Overall, car production rose steadily in Argentina and fell steadily in Australia. Thailand's figure climbed to a peak in 2006 before declining, although it remained the highest in all three years. Argentina also overtook Australia by 2006.

In 2003, Argentina made 235,088 cars, compared with 452,163 in Australia and 735,852 in Thailand. By 2006, the figure for Argentina had risen to 352,759, slightly above Australia's 341,268 after the latter country's output declined. Thailand saw a much larger increase, reaching a peak of 1,162,356 cars in the same year.

From 2006 to 2009, production in Australia continued to fall, ending at 245,624 cars. Thailand's figure also declined by 162,393 vehicles to 999,963, but it was still more than double Argentina's total. By contrast, the number of cars made in Argentina rose further from 352,759 to 466,089, making it the only country whose production increased in both intervals.

reviews.overall: Em đã viết đúng chủ đề, đủ số từ và có bốn đoạn. Tuy nhiên, bài này em soát chưa kỹ: biểu đồ nam chạm đáy năm 1931, không phải 1941, và kết thúc gần 46.000 người, không phải 85.000. Đoạn Overview cũng nói nữ giảm ở cuối kỳ, trong khi số nữ tăng từ 1971 đến 2001. Cô yêu cầu em đọc lại từng trục số, sửa các mốc chính và kiểm tra cách viết đại lượng, hòa hợp chủ ngữ–động từ, dấu câu trước khi nộp lại.
reviews.dataGrouping: Em dùng bốn đoạn và bắt đầu Detail bằng số liệu của nam, rồi nhắc đến nữ; đoạn cuối lại mô tả cả hai giới. Vì hai giới không có cùng một mốc đảo chiều nổi bật, em nên dành một Detail cho nam và một Detail cho nữ, mỗi đoạn ít nhất hai câu. Cách này giúp em nêu đúng đáy, bước nhảy và điểm cuối của từng đường, đồng thời so sánh số người theo hai trục tung khác nhau.

The given two line charts illustrate the prison population in a European country in a 90-years period, commencing from 1911.  
Overall, there was an increase in the number of male prisoners, evenwhile the number of female prisoners had a gradual drop at the end of the period. Also of note is that male prison population TOTAL consistently had the higher figures throughout the years.  
To elaborate, in 1911, approximately 20000 men was imprisoned in a European country, with a slight downturn to around 10000 male prisoners in 1941, marking the lowest point of the entire chart. The figures for female also went down significantly, from 4000 to under 1000 prisoners in the same period of time.  
Regarding categories with higher data, the number of prison population in both sex increased during the remaining time of the period. A dramatic growth was seen in the figures for male prisoners, from a mere 10 thousand to 1941 to around 85 thousand between 1941 and 2001. Finally, the number of female prison increased to nearly 2000 prisoners, this number was still below those of male.

The two line charts compare the numbers of male and female prisoners in a European country over the 90 years from 1911 to 2001.

Overall, male prisoners outnumbered female prisoners throughout the period. The male total fell early on before rising sharply, particularly between 1971 and 1981. By contrast, the female total dropped steeply until 1941, then fluctuated and ended below its initial level.

In 1911, the number of male prisoners stood at about 18,000, and it was similar in 1921. It then fell to roughly 10,000 in 1931, its lowest point. The figure then climbed to around 1,500 in 1961, fell to about 700 in 1971, and rose again to nearly 1,900 by 2001. Even at that point, it remained far lower than the number of male prisoners.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given line chart illustrates how much the consumption of fish and four different kinds of meat in a European country in a 25-year period, commencing from 1979.
Overall, out of the studied kinds of meat, only chicken witnessed signs of growth in people's consumption of it. Also of note is that fish consistently recorded lowest figures throughout the years.
To elaborate, starting at the leading position of the entire chart, approximate 225 grams, the amount of chicken eaten went up unsignificantly by 25 grams after 25 years. The figures for beef, otherwise, increase from under 150 grams to around 200 in the same period of time; the figure for beef, otherwise decrease from under 150 grams to around 100 grams in the same time, despite a progressively rise to around 200 grams in 1989.
Regarding categories with lower data, in 1979, exactly 150 grams of lamb used by per person per week and this number had a downward trend, dropped by a half of the begining to 75 gram in 1994 and continued to fell to around 50 gram in 2004. The figures for fish kept around 50 grams in 15 years, from 1979 to 1994 before decreasing to nearly 35 grams in 2004, marking the lowest point of the whole graph.

The line chart shows the weekly consumption of chicken, beef, lamb and fish, measured in grams per person, in a European country from 1979 to 2004.

Overall, chicken was the only category whose consumption increased substantially. It overtook beef around 1988–1989 and had the highest figure by 2004, whereas beef and lamb declined markedly. Fish remained the least consumed food throughout the period and fell only slightly.

In 1979, beef consumption was the highest at about 220 grams per person per week, compared with approximately 140 grams for chicken. Beef then peaked at nearly 240 grams in the early 1980s before falling, with some fluctuations, to around 110 grams in 2004. By contrast, chicken consumption rose with minor fluctuations to about 250 grams, an increase of roughly 110 grams over the period.

Regarding the remaining categories, lamb started at about 150 grams per person per week and generally declined to around 75 grams in 1994, followed by a further fall to roughly 55 grams in 2004. Fish began at approximately 60 grams, hovered around 40–50 grams for much of the period, and finished at about 35 grams.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given line chart illustrates the proportion of female members of parliament in five European countries over a 12-year period, commencing from 2000.  
Overall, out of the studied nations, only Belgium witnessed signs of a decline in its share of female parliamentary representation. Despite this, Germany had the highest figures throughout the years.  
To elaborate, in 2000, an impressive 33% of the total parliament members in Germany was reported at this level. This number, however, fell slightly to around 32% before recovering gradually to about 35% in 2012, thereby allowing this nation to maintain its leading position until the final studied year.  
Regarding the remaining options, the most noticeable upturn was seen in the UK, rising from around 3% in 2000 to an significant 23% after 12 years. The figures for France also grew from 16% to more or less 36% for the same period of time, yet they remained at a steady pattern near the end. The figures for Belgium and Italy, conversely, went up by roughly 2% and 12% respectively over the whole time

Belgium rose from 17% to 28%, while Italy's figure grew from 26% to 39%, overtaking Germany to finish first.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given pie charts illustrate the proportion of students choosing a particular university in the UK for different reasons in two different years, 1997 and 2007.  
Overall, out of the studied reasons, only suitable degree courses witnessed signs of a decline in its popularity. Despite this, suitable degree courses had the highest figures throughout the years.  
To elaborate, in 1997, an impressive 35% of the total students chose the university because of suitable degree courses. This number, however, fell significantly to 22% in around 2007. In 1997, quality of resources was recorded at 21%, thereby allowing this category to maintain its leading position until the final studied year, reaching 22% in 2007.  
Regarding the remaining options, the most noticeable upturn was seen in good sports and social activities, rising from around 10% in 1997 to an significant 17% after a decade, marking its second only to suitable degree courses and quality of resources in terms of student preferences. The figures for proximity to parental home also grew from 15% to more or less 18% for the same period of time. The figures for quality of teaching, conversely, went up by roughly 3%, from 19% to 22%, respectively over the whole time. Yet, they remained at relatively lower levels over the entire chart compared to the dominant drivers.

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The two pie charts show how students in the UK selected a particular university for five different reasons in 1997 and 2007.

Overall, the percentages of students who cited suitable degree courses, proximity to their parents' home or teaching quality rose, whereas the percentages for resources and sports and social activities fell. Suitable courses were the leading reason in both years; proximity to home was the least common in 1997, while sports and social activities ranked last in 2007.

To elaborate, in 1997, 35% of students chose the university because of its suitable degree courses, compared with 21% citing the quality of its resources. The former figure edged up to 37% in 2007 and remained the highest. By contrast, the share of students citing resources declined to 17%, falling below that for proximity to home.

Regarding the remaining reasons, 19% of students cited sports and social activities in 1997, but this proportion fell sharply to 6% in 2007. Proximity to parents' home showed the largest increase, from 10% to 22%, overtaking both resources and teaching quality. The proportion of students citing teaching quality also rose, though more modestly, from 15% to 18%.
